questions.explanation: Moving electric charges produce a magnetic field, so the coil and nail form an electromagnet. Disconnecting the battery stops the current and the magnetism.

questions.stem: A straw in a glass of water looks bent at the water's surface. What causes this?
options: The straw absorbs light under water
Light reflects off the bottom of the glass of water
The water dissolves part of the straw
Light bends as it passes between water and air
questions.explanation: Light bends (refracts) when it moves from one material into another at an angle, because its speed changes. Reflection is light bouncing back, which does not make the straw look broken.

questions.stem: Sodium and potassium both have one electron in their outermost energy level. What does this suggest about them?
options: They do not react with other elements
They have the same number of protons
questions.explanation: An element's chemical behavior depends mostly on its outermost electrons, so elements with the same number react alike. That is why both are reactive metals in the same column of the periodic table.

questions.stem: What happened to the amount of sand washed out as the tilt increased?
questions.explanation: The sand collected rose from 40 g at 5 degrees to 240 g at 20 degrees, a steady increase.

questions.stem: Based on the results, where would a real stream most likely erode its banks fastest?
options: Where it widens into a lake
Where it crosses a wide, flat valley floor
Where it flows down a steep hillside
questions.explanation: Steeper slopes made water move sand faster in the model, so a stream on a steep hillside would erode more than one on flat ground.

questions.stem: Two plates of Earth's crust are pulling apart under the ocean. What most likely forms there?
options: A tall mountain range from crashing plates
A fault where plates slide past
A deep trench where crust sinks
A ridge where new crust forms
questions.explanation: At diverging plates, magma rises and forms new ocean crust along a mid-ocean ridge. Trenches form where plates converge and one sinks.

questions.stem: Why does the Moon appear to change shape over about a month?
options: We see more or less of its sunlit half
Clouds hide different parts of it
The Moon makes its own light, which flickers
Earth's shadow covers different parts of it
questions.explanation: Half the Moon is always lit by the Sun. As it orbits Earth, we see more or less of that lit half. Earth's shadow falls on the Moon only during a lunar eclipse.

questions.stem: In undisturbed layers of sedimentary rock, fossils in the lowest layer are usually:
options: younger than fossils in the layers above
older than fossils in the layers above
the same age as all the other fossils
from animals that lived in the air
questions.explanation: Sediment builds up from the bottom, so in undisturbed rock the lowest layers formed first. This is the principle of superposition.

questions.stem: In the excerpt, "Four score and seven years ago" refers to:
options: the writing of the Bill of Rights
the start of the Civil War
the end of the Revolutionary War
questions.explanation: A score is 20, so four score and seven is 87 years. Lincoln spoke in 1863, and 87 years earlier was 1776, the year of the Declaration of Independence.

questions.stem: According to the excerpt, what is the Civil War testing?
options: Whether slavery can spread to new states
Whether a nation built on liberty can last
Whether Britain will support the Union side
Whether the North can win more battles
questions.explanation: Lincoln says the war is "testing whether that nation ... can long endure," meaning whether a nation based on liberty and equality can last.

questions.stem: In the late 1800s, large companies such as Standard Oil gained control of whole industries. Congress responded with laws against:
options: labor unions that raised wages for workers
questions.explanation: The Sherman Antitrust Act of 1890 targeted trusts and monopolies that crushed competition. Standard Oil was later broken up under that law.

questions.stem: Which event set off World War I in 1914?
options: The fall of the Berlin Wall
The sinking of the Titanic in the Atlantic
The killing of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
questions.explanation: The killing of Austria-Hungary's heir in Sarajevo led alliances across Europe into war. Pearl Harbor brought the United States into World War II.

questions.stem: Which event led the United States to enter World War II in December 1941?
options: The start of the Great Depression
The dropping of the atomic bomb
questions.explanation: Japan attacked the U.S. naval base at Pearl Harbor on December 7, 1941, and Congress declared war the next day. Germany invaded Poland in 1939, before the United States joined.

questions.stem: In Brown v. Board of Education (1954), the Supreme Court ruled that:
options: women had the right to vote
states could still require separate but equal schools
questions.explanation: Brown overturned the "separate but equal" idea for public schools, holding that segregated schools violated the Fourteenth Amendment's equal protection clause.

questions.stem: Ancient Athens is best known for developing an early form of:
questions.explanation: In Athens, male citizens voted directly on laws in an assembly, an early democracy. Feudalism belongs to medieval Europe, and communism to the modern era.

questions.stem: Which age group had the highest turnout in the table?
questions.explanation: Voters 65 and older turned out at 71%, the highest share in the table.

questions.stem: Which conclusion is best supported by the table?
options: Turnout rose with each older age group
Turnout was the same in every age group
Most young people do not care about politics
questions.explanation: Each older group voted at a higher rate, from 38% up to 71%. The table shows who voted, not why young people stayed home or whom anyone chose.

questions.stem: Which amendment protects the right to vote from being denied because of sex?
questions.explanation: The Nineteenth Amendment, ratified in 1920, protected women's right to vote. The Twenty-second limits presidents to two elected terms.

questions.stem: The power of federal courts to strike down a law that conflicts with the Constitution is called:
questions.explanation: Judicial review was established in Marbury v. Madison (1803). An executive order comes from the president, a filibuster is a Senate tactic, and impeachment is a power of Congress.

questions.stem: Under Article V, a proposed amendment is most often added to the Constitution when it is approved by two-thirds of both houses of Congress and then:
options: approved by a majority of the Supreme Court
ratified by three-fourths of the states
questions.explanation: Article V requires ratification by three-fourths of the states. The president plays no formal role, and there is no national vote.

questions.stem: Which level of government usually decides where a new shopping center may be built?
questions.explanation: Zoning, the rules on what may be built where, is handled mainly by city and county governments.

questions.stem: What is the main difference between a republic and an absolute monarchy?
options: A monarchy always has an elected national legislature
In a republic, leaders are chosen by the people
In a republic, the ruler inherits power
A monarchy has no laws at all
questions.explanation: In a republic, citizens elect representatives to govern. In an absolute monarchy, a king or queen inherits power and rules without being elected.

questions.stem: Which statement from the editorial is an opinion?
options: Prices have risen by about 12 percent.
It is unfair to ask every family to pay for it.
The tariff applies to imported washing machines.
questions.explanation: Whether the cost is "unfair" is the writer's judgment. The tariff rate, the price rise and what the tariff covers can be checked.

questions.stem: Based on the editorial, how did the tariff affect consumers?
options: They could no longer buy washing machines
They paid less for washing machines
They earned more at factory jobs
They paid more for washing machines
questions.explanation: The editorial says local washer prices rose about 12 percent after the tariff. A tariff is a tax on imports, which tends to raise prices.

questions.stem: When prices are rising too fast, the Federal Reserve usually raises interest rates. How does this help?
options: Borrowing costs more, so spending slows
Banks print more money to lend to businesses
questions.explanation: Higher rates make loans more expensive, so people and businesses borrow and spend less, easing the pressure on prices. Taxes are fiscal policy, set by Congress.

questions.stem: Why does a borrower with a high credit score usually get a lower interest rate?
options: They have more money in savings
Lenders expect them to repay on time
The law requires their rate to be set lower
questions.explanation: A credit score reflects how reliably someone has repaid debts. Lower risk to the lender earns a lower rate.

questions.stem: A climograph shows a city with hot temperatures all year and heavy rain in every month. The city most likely has which climate?
questions.explanation: Year-round heat and rain describe a tropical rain forest climate near the equator. A desert is dry, a polar climate is cold, and a Mediterranean climate has dry summers.

questions.stem: Sushi restaurants opening in cities far from Japan is an example of:
questions.explanation: Cultural diffusion is the spread of ideas, foods and customs from one place to another.

questions.stem: Why does Ellen climb the lighthouse alone on this night?
options: Her father is sick with a fever
She wants to prove she is grown
Her father has gone out with the boats
questions.explanation: The story says her father "lay in bed with a fever" as the storm came in, so she offers to light the lamp herself.

questions.stem: The wind is described as pushing "against the tower like a shoulder against a door." This comparison emphasizes the wind's:
questions.explanation: A shoulder against a door is a heavy, steady push, showing the force Ellen faces as she climbs.

questions.stem: What keeps Ellen climbing after her lantern gutters?
options: A promise she had made to a fisherman in the harbor
Thinking of the people who depend on the light
Hope of seeing the storm up close
questions.explanation: Standing in the dark, she thinks of the boats, the men in the harbor and their waiting wives, and then "She climbed."

questions.stem: The final sentence, in which distant lights turn "toward home," suggests that:
options: other keepers have lit their own towers
Ellen's father has come up the stairs
the boats can now find their way safely
questions.explanation: The beam swings out and boats answer and turn toward home, showing that Ellen's light is guiding them to safety.

questions.stem: According to the passage, what are expansion joints for?
options: Letting a bridge deck lengthen and shorten
Holding the deck firmly in place on its supports
questions.explanation: The passage says the joint "leaves a gap that can open and close as the deck moves," so the deck can grow and shrink with temperature.

questions.stem: According to the passage, what would happen to a deck fixed solidly at both ends?
options: It would sag in the middle each summer
It would crack or buckle under the force
It would shrink until the ends pulled loose
It would bounce whenever a truck crossed
questions.explanation: With nowhere to expand, the material "would push against the supports with enormous force, cracking concrete or buckling steel."

questions.stem: Why does a long bridge move several inches when one foot of steel changes only a tiny amount?
options: Traffic stretches the deck over time
Long bridges are built from a weaker kind of steel
The small change adds up over the full length
Concrete expands much more than steel
questions.explanation: The passage explains that the change per foot is tiny, but a deck hundreds or thousands of feet long adds those changes together.

questions.stem: Which statement best expresses the main idea of the passage?
options: Bridges are bumpy because of poor building
Steel is a poor choice for long bridges
Expansion joints are needed only on very long bridges
Gaps let structures handle heat and cold safely
questions.explanation: The passage explains why materials expand and contract and how gaps in bridges, tracks and buildings let them do so without damage.

questions.stem: [1] The writer is considering deleting the underlined sentence. Should the writer make this deletion?
options: Yes, because it is about phones, not bikes
Yes, because it only repeats the number of bikes and stations
No, because it gives the cost of a ride
No, because it explains how the program works
questions.explanation: Readers need to know how bike share works before the report discusses its use, and this sentence explains it.

questions.stem: [2] Why does the underlined sentence work as the opening of paragraph 2?
options: It states the point the trip numbers then support
It contrasts the program with buses
It introduces the problems with stations running out of bikes
It gives the date the program started
questions.explanation: "Use has grown steadily" is the paragraph's main point, and the trip counts that follow are the evidence.

questions.stem: [3] Which choice is best for the underlined portion?
questions.explanation: The paragraph calls the growth steady, so the plain "rose" fits. "Exploded wildly" exaggerates, "rose upward" repeats itself, and "exploding" cannot be the sentence's verb.

questions.stem: [4] Which choice is the best first sentence for paragraph 3?
options: Some stations are near a lake.
The bike app can be used in four different languages.
Riders often use the bikes as part of a longer trip.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 explains that riders use the bikes to reach buses and trains, so a sentence about longer trips introduces it. The color of the bikes is beside the point.

questions.stem: [5] Which choice is best for the underlined portion?
options: For these riders, the bikes fill a gap: the last mile
For these riders the bikes fill a gap the last mile
For these riders, the bikes fill a gap. The last mile
questions.explanation: A colon introduces the phrase that names the gap. A semicolon must join two complete sentences, and "the last mile between transit and home" is not one; a period would leave that phrase as a fragment.

questions.stem: [6] Which choice is best for the underlined portion?
questions.explanation: The report turns from the program's success to its problems, a contrast that "However" signals. "Therefore" signals a result, "For example" an example and "Likewise" a similarity.

questions.stem: [7] Which choice is best for the underlined portion?
questions.explanation: "The city" is singular, so it takes "has hired." "Have," "were" and "are" are plural forms.

questions.stem: [8] Which choice is best for the underlined portion?
options: Each of the stations have needed more docks
Each of the stations are needing more docks
Each of the stations needs more docks
questions.explanation: The subject is "Each," which is singular, so the verb is "needs." "Stations" is part of the phrase that follows it.

questions.stem: [9] Which choice is best for the underlined portion?
options: The report recommends adding twenty stations, and it also recommends using discounts.
Adding twenty stations is recommended, and also discounts, by the report.
The report, recommending twenty stations, discounts are also used.
questions.explanation: The draft gives both recommendations in one clear sentence. Repeating "recommends" adds words, and the passive and dangling versions are confusing or ungrammatical.

questions.stem: [1] Which choice is best for the underlined portion?
options: As a child, I was too scared; as an adult, I was too embarrassed.
As a child, I was too scared, and as an adult, too embarrassed, I was.
As a child I was too scared as an adult I was too embarrassed.
questions.explanation: The draft joins two sentences with a comma. A semicolon separates them and keeps the balanced contrast. Dropping all punctuation makes a run-on, and "too embarrassed, I was" is awkward.

questions.stem: [2] How does the underlined sentence help paragraph 2?
options: It explains why the writer chose this pool and instructor
It sets up the fear the paragraph then describes
It tells how long the lessons lasted
questions.explanation: The paragraph goes on to describe clinging to the side of the pool, which shows how frightening the first lesson was.

questions.stem: [3] Which choice is best for the underlined portion?
options: She taught me to float, first she said
She taught me to float first. She said
She taught me to float first, and saying
questions.explanation: Two complete sentences are joined by only a comma. A period separates them. "And saying" leaves the second part without a subject, and moving "first" keeps the comma splice.

questions.stem: [4] Which choice is the best first sentence for paragraph 3?
options: Many pools have a deep end.
Grace once swam across a very large lake.
Slowly, the lessons began to work.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 traces the writer's progress week by week, so a sentence about the lessons starting to work introduces it. How pools are cleaned is off topic.

questions.stem: [5] Which choice is best for the underlined portion?
options: Two other adult students and I
Myself and two other adult students
Two other adult students and me
questions.explanation: The pronoun is part of the subject, so it takes the subject form "I." "Me" and "myself" are not used as subjects.

questions.stem: [6] Which choice is best for the underlined portion?
questions.explanation: The paragraph steps back from the lessons to sum up what they meant, which "In the end" signals. "For example" and "For instance" introduce an example, and "In contrast" a difference.

questions.stem: [7] Which choice is best for the underlined portion?
options: Its a lesson that I apply, now, to every new thing that I try.
It's a lesson I now try to apply and use for new things I try.
It's a lesson I now try to apply to everything new.
questions.explanation: "Apply" and "use" mean the same here, and "try ... try" repeats a word. The short version keeps the meaning. "Its" without an apostrophe is the possessive, not "it is."

questions.stem: [8] Why does the underlined sentence work as an ending?
options: It gives the instructor's name again to end the story
It explains how pools are cleaned
It returns to the ocean from the first paragraph
It lists the other adult students
questions.explanation: The essay opens by saying the writer grew up near the ocean but could not swim, so planning to swim in it brings the story full circle.

questions.stem: [9] Which choice is best for the underlined portion?
options: I am excited, a little nervous and ready.
I am excited and nervous and ready and I am.
Excited, I am, and nervous, and ready.
questions.explanation: Listing the three feelings after one "I am" says the same thing without repeating the subject and verb. The other versions repeat words or scramble the order.

questions.stem: What is $\frac{2}{3}$ of $\frac{3}{4}$ of 48?
questions.explanation: $\frac{3}{4}$ of 48 is 36, and $\frac{2}{3}$ of 36 is 24. Stopping after the first step gives 36, and $\frac{2}{3}$ of 48 is 32.

questions.stem: What is $1\frac{1}{2} + 2\frac{3}{4}$?
questions.explanation: Use a common denominator: $1\frac{2}{4} + 2\frac{3}{4} = 3\frac{5}{4} = 4\frac{1}{4}$. Adding tops and bottoms gives $\frac{4}{6}$, and forgetting to carry the extra whole gives $3\frac{1}{4}$.

questions.stem: 18 is what percent of 72?
questions.explanation: $\frac{18}{72} = 0.25$, or 25%. Dividing 72 by 18 gives 4, and subtracting gives 54.

questions.stem: What is $\frac{6.0 \times 10^8}{1.5 \times 10^3}$ in scientific notation?
questions.explanation: Divide the numbers and subtract the exponents: $6.0 \div 1.5 = 4.0$ and $10^{8-3} = 10^5$. Adding the exponents gives $10^{11}$.

questions.stem: How many inches are in 3.5 feet?
questions.explanation: There are 12 inches in a foot: $3.5 \times 12 = 42$. Treating a foot as 10 inches gives 35.

questions.stem: A paint mix uses 2 parts blue to 5 parts white. How many quarts of blue are in 21 quarts of the mix?
questions.explanation: The mix has $2 + 5 = 7$ parts, so each part is $21 \div 7 = 3$ quarts and blue is $2 \times 3 = 6$. 15 quarts is the white, and 8.4 treats blue as $\frac{2}{5}$ of the mix.

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $\frac{x^8}{x^2}$?
questions.explanation: When dividing powers with the same base, subtract the exponents: $8 - 2 = 6$. Dividing the exponents gives $x^4$, and adding them gives $x^{10}$.

questions.stem: Concert tickets cost \$18.50 each. Dev buys 4 tickets and uses a \$5 coupon on the whole order. How much does he pay?
questions.explanation: Four tickets cost $4 \times 18.50 = 74$, and the coupon takes off 5, so he pays \$69. Forgetting the coupon gives \$74, and adding it gives \$79.

questions.stem: A rectangular floor is 14 feet long and 9.5 feet wide. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Area is length times width: $14 \times 9.5 = 133$. Adding the sides twice gives 47, which is the perimeter.

questions.stem: A rectangle has an area of 48 square inches and a length of 8 inches. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: The width is $48 \div 8 = 6$, so the perimeter is $2(8 + 6) = 28$. Adding just one length and one width gives 14.

questions.stem: A circular table has a diameter of 14 inches. About how far is it around the edge?
questions.explanation: Circumference is $\pi d = 14\pi \approx 44$. Using the radius as the diameter gives 22, and 154 is the area, $\pi r^2$.

questions.stem: Two angles of a triangle measure 47 degrees and 68 degrees. What is the measure of the third angle?
questions.explanation: The angles of a triangle add to 180: $180 - 47 - 68 = 65$. 115 is the sum of the two given angles.

questions.stem: Ana walks 9 blocks east and then 12 blocks north. How far is she from her starting point in a straight line?
questions.explanation: The path forms a right triangle: $\sqrt{9^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{225} = 15$. 21 is the distance walked, and 108 multiplies the legs.

questions.stem: A box is 12 inches long, 8 inches wide and 5 inches tall. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Volume is length times width times height: $12 \times 8 \times 5 = 480$. Adding the dimensions gives 25.

questions.stem: The point $(3, -2)$ is reflected across the $y$-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
questions.explanation: Reflecting across the $y$-axis changes the sign of the $x$-coordinate only. Reflecting across the $x$-axis would give $(3, 2)$.

questions.stem: Two straight lines cross. One of the four angles formed measures 38 degrees. What is the measure of an angle next to it?
questions.explanation: Angles next to each other along a straight line are supplementary: $180 - 38 = 142$. 38 is the vertical (opposite) angle, and 52 would make them complementary.

questions.stem: Omar's four test scores are 78, 85, 92 and 81. What is his mean score?
questions.explanation: Add the scores and divide by 4: $\frac{78 + 85 + 92 + 81}{4} = \frac{336}{4} = 84$. 83 is the median.

questions.stem: What is the median of 3, 8, 12, 5, 9, 15, 7?
questions.explanation: Put the values in order: 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, 12, 15. The middle of seven values is the fourth, 8. Taking the middle of the unsorted list gives 5.

questions.stem: A fair number cube is rolled. What is the probability of rolling a number greater than 4?
questions.explanation: Only 5 and 6 are greater than 4, so the probability is $\frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3}$. Counting 4 as well gives $\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.stem:
A shop recorded its sales.

| Month | Jan | Feb | Mar | Apr | May |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sales | 120 | 150 | 165 | 210 | 220 |

Which month had the greatest increase over the month before?
questions.explanation: The increases are 30 in February, 15 in March, 45 in April and 10 in May, so April had the greatest. May had the highest sales but the smallest increase.

questions.stem: A scatter plot shows that students who studied more hours tended to get higher test scores. Which describes this relationship?
questions.explanation: When one value tends to rise as the other rises, the association is positive. A negative one would show scores falling as study time rises.

questions.stem:
A survey of 100 adults asked about exercise and sleep.

| | Sleeps 7+ hours | Sleeps less | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Exercises | 45 | 15 | 60 |
| Does not | 20 | 20 | 40 |
| Total | 65 | 35 | 100 |

What percent of the adults who exercise sleep 7 or more hours?
questions.explanation: Of the 60 who exercise, 45 sleep 7 or more hours: $\frac{45}{60} = 75\%$. 45% divides by all 100 adults, and 69% divides by the 65 who sleep 7+ hours.

questions.stem: In a random sample of 200 voters, 120 support a new park. If the town has 15,000 voters, about how many would be expected to support it?
questions.explanation: The sample rate is $\frac{120}{200} = 60\%$, and 60% of 15,000 is 9,000. 6,000 is the share that does not support it.

questions.stem: The data set 12, 14, 15, 13, 46 includes an outlier, 46. What happens if 46 is removed?
options: The mean and median stay the same
The mean falls much more than the median
The median falls much more than the mean
The mean rises and the median falls
questions.explanation: The mean drops from 20 to 13.5, but the median only moves from 14 to 13.5. An outlier pulls the mean far more than the median.

questions.stem: What value of $x$ makes $7 - 2x = 15$ true?
questions.explanation: Subtract 7: $-2x = 8$. Divide by $-2$: $x = -4$. Check: $7 - 2(-4) = 15$. Dropping the negative gives 4.

questions.stem: A line crosses the $y$-axis at 3 and has a slope of $-2$. Which equation describes it?
questions.explanation: In slope-intercept form $y = mx + b$, $m$ is the slope and $b$ is the $y$-intercept, so $y = -2x + 3$. Swapping them gives $y = 3x - 2$.

questions.stem: A nurse tests whether a new bandage helps cuts heal faster. She records how many days each cut takes to heal. What is the dependent variable?
options: The number of days to heal
questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the result that is measured, the days to heal. The bandage type is the independent variable, the one being changed.

questions.stem: Researchers give a new vitamin to one group of people and a look-alike pill with no vitamin to another. Why give the second group the look-alike pill?
options: To make sure both groups get the vitamin
To keep the people in the first group from getting sick
To double the number of vitamins tested
To compare results against a group that got no vitamin
questions.explanation: The look-alike pill group is the control. Comparing the two groups shows whether changes came from the vitamin and not from just taking a pill.

questions.stem: What was the swing time for a string 2.25 meters long?
questions.explanation: The table pairs a length of 2.25 m with a swing time of 3.0 s.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the pattern in the data?
options: Making the string 4 times longer doubles the swing time
Doubling the string length doubles the swing time
Longer strings make the swing time shorter
The length of the string has no effect on the swing time
questions.explanation: From 0.25 m to 1.00 m (4 times longer) the time goes from 1.0 s to 2.0 s, and from 1.00 m to 4.00 m it goes from 2.0 s to 4.0 s. Each quadrupling doubles the time.

questions.stem: Why did the student pull the weight back by the same angle each time?
options: So that the string would not break
So that only the string length changed between trials
So that the weight would swing faster
So that each swing time would be longer and easier to time
questions.explanation: Keeping the angle the same makes string length the only variable that changed, so the differences in time can be linked to it.

questions.stem: When water boils, what happens to its molecules?
options: They break apart into hydrogen and oxygen atoms
They move faster and spread apart as a gas
They slow down and lock into place
questions.explanation: Heating gives molecules more energy, so they move faster and escape as water vapor. The molecules stay water; boiling is a physical change, not a chemical one.

questions.stem: In a sealed container, 10 grams of one substance react completely with 5 grams of another. What is the total mass of the products?
questions.explanation: Mass is conserved in a chemical reaction: atoms are rearranged, not created or destroyed, so the products have the same 15 grams as the reactants.

questions.stem: A metal spoon left in a pot of hot soup becomes hot at the handle. How did the heat reach the handle?
options: By radiation from the stove burner below
questions.explanation: Conduction moves heat through a solid as particles pass energy to their neighbors. Convection moves heat through flowing liquids and gases.

questions.stem: A cork floats in water but a rock of the same size sinks. What does this show?
options: The cork is less dense than water
The rock is less dense than water
The cork has more mass than the rock
questions.explanation: Objects less dense than water float, and denser objects sink. The cork and rock are the same size, so the rock has more mass in the same volume.

questions.stem: How long does Mars take to orbit the Sun?
questions.explanation: The table gives Mars's orbit time as 1.88 Earth years. 1.52 is its distance from the Sun in AU.

questions.stem: Which pattern do the data show?
options: Every planet takes one year to orbit
Orbit time does not depend on distance from the Sun
Planets farther from the Sun take longer to orbit
Closer planets take longer to orbit
questions.explanation: Orbit times rise with distance: 0.24 years for Mercury up to 11.9 years for Jupiter.

questions.stem: Saturn is about 9.5 AU from the Sun. Based on the table, its orbit time is most likely:
questions.explanation: Saturn is farther out than Jupiter, so by the pattern it takes longer than Jupiter's 11.9 years. Its actual orbit is about 29 years.

questions.stem: Which of these is a renewable resource?
questions.explanation: Wind keeps being produced by the Sun's uneven heating of Earth. Coal, natural gas and oil formed over millions of years and are used up far faster than they form.

questions.stem: Which process carries water from the ocean into the air?
questions.explanation: Evaporation turns liquid water into water vapor. Condensation forms clouds from vapor, precipitation brings water back down, and runoff carries it over land.

questions.stem: Most earthquakes and volcanoes occur:
options: only near the North and South Poles
near the edges of tectonic plates
in the middle of large plates, far from the edges
questions.explanation: Plate boundaries are where plates collide, pull apart or slide past each other, building up the stress that causes earthquakes and the melting that feeds volcanoes.

questions.stem: The Sun looks much brighter than other stars. What is the main reason?
options: It is the hottest star there is
It is the only star that gives off light
It is the largest star there is
It is much closer to Earth
questions.explanation: The Sun is an average star; it looks so bright because it is far closer than any other star. Many stars are larger and hotter.

questions.stem: Based on the timeline, which event came last?
options: The Voting Rights Act was passed
Women's right to vote was protected
Poll taxes were banned in federal elections
questions.explanation: The Twenty-sixth Amendment, in 1971, is the latest date on the timeline.

questions.stem: Which conclusion is best supported by the timeline?
options: Voting rights were set once and never changed
Voting rights grew over about 100 years
Every change was made by a court ruling
Only the states changed voting rules
questions.explanation: From 1870 to 1971, amendments and a federal law steadily extended voting to more citizens. Four of the five steps were constitutional amendments, and one was an act of Congress.

questions.stem: In 1803, the United States bought the Louisiana Territory from:
questions.explanation: President Jefferson bought the territory from Napoleon's France, roughly doubling the size of the country.

questions.stem: After World War II, the United States gave billions of dollars to help rebuild Western Europe under:
questions.explanation: The Marshall Plan funded European recovery, partly to keep communism from spreading. The New Deal was a domestic program of the 1930s.

questions.stem: In the Roman Republic, citizens elected officials to make decisions for them. This system is an early example of:
questions.explanation: Electing others to govern is representative government, the idea behind a republic. In direct democracy, citizens vote on laws themselves.

questions.stem: How long is the term of a member of the U.S. House of Representatives?
questions.explanation: House members serve two-year terms, senators six-year terms, and presidents four-year terms.

questions.stem: The Twenty-sixth Amendment set the national voting age at:
questions.explanation: Ratified in 1971, the Twenty-sixth Amendment protects the right of citizens 18 or older to vote. Before it, many states used 21.

questions.stem: Police want to search a person's home. Which amendment protects people from unreasonable searches?
questions.explanation: The Fourth Amendment protects against unreasonable searches and seizures and usually requires a warrant based on probable cause.

questions.stem: The clause that lets Congress make all laws "necessary and proper" for carrying out its listed powers is the basis of:
questions.explanation: Powers that are not listed but are needed to carry out listed powers are implied powers. Reserved powers belong to the states.

questions.stem: Which action is an example of informed participation in a democracy?
options: Sharing a rumor without checking it
Voting for whoever is listed first
Skipping elections for city and county offices
questions.explanation: Informed participation means learning about issues and candidates before acting. Voting by ballot order and spreading unchecked rumors are not informed choices.

questions.stem: In economics, scarcity means that:
options: a country has no natural resources
a product is no longer made
questions.explanation: Because resources are limited and wants are not, people must make choices. That is scarcity, the basic problem of economics.

questions.stem: A new study makes a fruit very popular, but the supply does not change. What will most likely happen to its price?
questions.explanation: Higher demand with the same supply means more buyers compete for the same amount, which pushes the price up.

questions.stem: The government cuts taxes and increases spending on roads to boost the economy. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Fiscal policy is the use of government taxing and spending. Monetary policy, such as changing interest rates, is run by the Federal Reserve.

questions.stem: Based on the map description, where do most people in the country live?
options: Along the coast and around river mouths
In the dry grassland east of the mountains
High in the mountains in the center
questions.explanation: The darkest shading, showing the most people, is along the coast and around two river mouths.

questions.stem: Which is the most likely reason few people live east of the mountains?
options: The coast is too crowded to reach
The land is dry, so farming and water are scarce
The mountains are near the ocean
The rivers flood the grassland every year
questions.explanation: The map labels the eastern land "dry grassland." Little water limits farming and settlement, while coasts and rivers offer water, trade and fertile land.

questions.stem: Which describes the absolute location of a place?
options: Its distance from the nearest city
questions.explanation: Absolute location is an exact position, given by latitude and longitude. Describing a place by what is near it is relative location.
